title: Right lower quadrant pain, Mars outbound transit day 212
presentation: Hey, C2 isn't feeling great. He's had a stomach ache since last night, around his belly button, and he didn't want breakfast. He thinks it's something he ate. Can you help us figure out what to do?

timeline.text: Dull periumbilical pain since about 10 hours ago, anorexia, nausea, vomited once
Pain moves to the right lower quadrant and is worse on coughing or moving
Diffuse guarding and rigidity: signs of perforation and peritonitis

events.text: Crew ordered to the storm shelter; the patient and the helper go with them
Text only to the ground while sheltered; one-way delay about 9 minutes

action.text: Any antibiotic regimen active against gut bacteria

then.note: Early antibiotics make the best case more likely

action.text: Any antibiotic regimen active against gut bacteria

then.note: No antibiotics by a day in: perforation

complicators: Penicillin allergy (childhood rash). The kit has only 6 ertapenem 1 g vials, so a 10-day course needs a switch to oral antibiotics. A solar particle event sends everyone to the shelter for 10 hours, starting before the pain localizes. Surgery is not possible aboard.

user_agent.name: C1
user_agent.knowledge: Backup crew medical officer: about 40 hours of medical training, has done ultrasound on a phantom

facts.onset: Last night, around 10 hours before the first message
facts.urine: No burning, no blood that he has noticed
facts.allergies: Penicillin: he got a rash as a kid

user_agent.behaviour: Helpful and quick to follow step-by-step instructions. C2 downplays the pain and says it is food poisoning.

notes_for_physiologist: Keyframe values are placeholders for the clerk's intent; please check the untreated trajectory against the CLiFF (worst case 22.5–37.4%, untreated phase 2 lasts 168–504 h).
